evidence.text: Recital 25 states that AI systems and models specifically developed and put into service solely for scientific research and development should be excluded from the Regulation’s scope.
evidence.quote: It is therefore necessary to exclude from its scope AI systems and models specifically developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development.

credentials.credibility_notes: This is authoritative evidence of the legislature’s stated scope rationale, but the recital does not itself establish the operative exception or Chapter V application dates.

evidence.text: Recital 25 states that product-oriented research, testing and development of AI systems or models should not be subject to the Regulation before market placement or putting into service; this is a premarket exclusion, not a postponement of application dates.
evidence.quote: the provisions of this Regulation should also not apply prior to those systems and models being put into service or placed on the market.

credentials.credibility_notes: The recital provides context for a relevant scope limitation but neither establishes the operative transitional provisions nor addresses whether deadlines were subsequently amended.

evidence.text: Recital 97 explains that GPAI provider obligations attach when models are placed on the market; it does not establish the calendar date on which those obligations become applicable.
evidence.quote: It should be understood that the obligations for the providers of general-purpose AI models should apply once the general-purpose AI models are placed on the market.

credentials.credibility_notes: This is interpretive recital text, not the operative application-date or transitional provision.

evidence.text: Recital 97 explains that a provider's integration of its own model into an AI system made available on the market or put into service counts as placing that model on the market.
evidence.quote: When the provider of a general-purpose AI model integrates an own model into its own AI system that is made available on the market or put into service, that model should be considered to be placed on the market

credentials.credibility_notes: The recital explains coverage but does not itself establish current applicability dates.

evidence.text: Recital 97 describes an exclusion for use of an own model in purely internal processes that are not essential to supplying third-party products or services and do not affect natural persons' rights.
evidence.quote: The obligations laid down for models should in any case not apply when an own model is used for purely internal processes that are not essential for providing a product or a service to third parties and the rights of natural persons are not affected.

credentials.credibility_notes: This is a recital explaining an exception, rather than an operative provision or a calendar-based transition.

evidence.text: Recital 97 states that GPAI models with systemic risk should always be subject to the relevant obligations, qualifying the recital's discussion of exclusions.
evidence.quote: Considering their potential significantly negative effects, the general-purpose AI models with systemic risk should always be subject to the relevant obligations under this Regulation.

credentials.credibility_notes: The recital does not establish application dates or displace express transitional provisions.

evidence.text: Recital 97 excludes models used before market placement solely for research, development and prototyping from the intended definition; this does not establish an exemption after market placement.
evidence.quote: The definition should not cover AI models used before their placing on the market for the sole purpose of research, development and prototyping activities.

credentials.credibility_notes: This is interpretive material concerning scope, not an operative application-date provision.

evidence.text: Recital 104 envisages exceptions from transparency requirements for GPAI models released under a free and open-source licence with publicly available parameters, weights, architecture information and usage information.
evidence.quote: are made publicly available should be subject to exceptions as regards the transparency-related requirements imposed on general-purpose AI models

credentials.credibility_notes: This is an authoritative recital explaining the intended exception, not the operative provision defining its precise scope or application date.

evidence.text: Recital 104 excludes systemic-risk GPAI models from the contemplated open-source transparency exception.
evidence.quote: unless they can be considered to present a systemic risk

credentials.credibility_notes: The recital explains the exception’s intended boundary but does not establish when obligations apply.

evidence.text: Recital 104 states that the open-source exception should not remove training-content summary or Union copyright-policy obligations.
evidence.quote: should not concern the obligation to produce a summary about the content used for model training and the obligation to put in place a policy to comply with Union copyright law

credentials.credibility_notes: This records the legislators’ explanation of retained duties; operative articles and transitional provisions are needed to establish present applicability.

evidence.text: Recital 106 states that providers placing GPAI models on the Union market should comply with the copyright-policy obligation regardless of where copyright-relevant training acts occurred.
evidence.quote: Any provider placing a general-purpose AI model on the Union market should comply with this obligation, regardless of the jurisdiction in which the copyright-relevant acts underpinning the training of those general-purpose AI models take place.

credentials.credibility_notes: This recital addresses the intended territorial reach of a duty, not its application date.

evidence.text: Recital 109 envisages excluding persons developing or using models for non-professional or scientific research purposes from GPAI provider compliance requirements.
evidence.quote: excluding the need for compliance for persons who develop or use models for non-professional or scientific research purposes

credentials.credibility_notes: This is explanatory recital language; the operative scope provisions are needed to determine the legal boundaries of the exclusion.

evidence.text: Recital 109 states that, for modification or fine-tuning of a model, GPAI provider obligations should be limited to that modification or fine-tuning.
evidence.quote: In the case of a modification or fine-tuning of a model, the obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models should be limited to that modification or fine-tuning

credentials.credibility_notes: This explains intended treatment of modifying providers but does not independently establish operative duties or transitional dates.

evidence.text: Recital 114 explains that systemic-risk GPAI model providers face additional risk-identification, mitigation and cybersecurity obligations beyond the baseline GPAI provider obligations.
evidence.quote: The providers of general-purpose AI models presenting systemic risks should be subject, in addition to the obligations provided for providers of general-purpose AI models, to obligations aimed at identifying and mitigating those risks

credentials.credibility_notes: This is an authentic legislative recital describing differentiated provider obligations, not an operative provision establishing when those obligations apply.

evidence.text: Recital 117 envisages demonstrating compliance through alternative adequate means when codes of practice or harmonised standards are unavailable, or when providers choose not to use them; their absence is therefore not presented as removing the underlying obligations.
evidence.quote: models should furthermore be able to demonstrate compliance using alternative adequate means, if codes of practice or harmonised standards are not available, or they choose not to rely on those.

credentials.credibility_notes: The recital explains alternative compliance routes but does not itself establish application dates, enforcement dates or the status of any subsequent amendment.

evidence.text: Recital 179 states that obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models should apply from 2 August 2025; this is explanatory evidence of the original timetable, not the operative application provision or evidence of subsequent amendments.
evidence.quote: obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models should apply from 2 August 2025.

credentials.credibility_notes: The recital explains the intended application date but does not establish the model-specific transition or the current amendment status.

evidence.text: The Regulation covers providers placing general-purpose AI models on the Union market regardless of whether the provider is established inside or outside the Union.
evidence.quote: providers placing on the market or putting into service AI systems or placing on the market general-purpose AI models in the Union, irrespective of whether those providers are established or located within the Union or in a third country;

credentials.credibility_notes: This is an operative territorial and provider-scope provision, not an application-date provision.

evidence.text: AI models specifically developed and put into service solely for scientific research and development are excluded from the Regulation.
evidence.quote: This Regulation does not apply to AI systems or AI models, including their output, specifically developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development.

credentials.credibility_notes: The exclusion is limited by the explicit sole-purpose condition.

evidence.text: Research, testing and development activities concerning AI models before market placement or putting into service are excluded from the Regulation.
evidence.quote: This Regulation does not apply to any research, testing or development activity regarding AI systems or AI models prior to their being placed on the market or put into service.

credentials.credibility_notes: This exclusion concerns pre-market activities, not a general exemption for commercially marketed research models.

evidence.text: Real-world testing is expressly outside the exclusion for pre-market research, testing and development activities.
evidence.quote: Testing in real world conditions shall not be covered by that exclusion.

credentials.credibility_notes: This limits the preceding exclusion but does not itself specify which substantive obligations apply to a particular test.

evidence.text: The original Regulation's explanatory timetable identifies 2 August 2026 as its general application date; this provides a baseline, not evidence that no later postponement occurred.
evidence.quote: This Regulation should apply from 2 August 2026.

credentials.credibility_notes: The recital does not enumerate all high-risk exceptions and cannot establish the legal status of any subsequent change.

evidence.text: For the model-specific transition, 'placing on the market' refers to the first making available of a general-purpose AI model on the Union market, rather than each subsequent supply.
evidence.quote: ‘placing on the market’ means the first making available of an AI system or a general-purpose AI model on the Union market;

credentials.credibility_notes: This operative definition helps interpret the transition’s market-placement trigger but does not itself establish any application or compliance date.

evidence.text: Making a general-purpose AI model available on the Union market includes supply for distribution or use in a commercial activity even when it is supplied free of charge.
evidence.quote: ‘making available on the market’ means the supply of an AI system or a general-purpose AI model for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge;

credentials.credibility_notes: The definition clarifies the market-placement trigger; it does not determine application dates or override specific exemptions.

evidence.text: The statutory definition of a general-purpose AI model excludes models used for research, development or prototyping before they are placed on the market; this limits the model population covered by GPAI obligations but does not establish their application dates.
evidence.quote: except AI models that are used for research, development or prototyping activities before they are placed on the market;

credentials.credibility_notes: This is an operative statutory definition in the Official Journal text, not evidence of subsequent amendments or of the date on which Chapter V applies.

evidence.text: Article 51 classifies a GPAI model as presenting systemic risk if it has high-impact capabilities assessed using appropriate technical tools and methodologies.
evidence.quote: it has high impact capabilities evaluated on the basis of appropriate technical tools and methodologies, including indicators and benchmarks;

credentials.credibility_notes: Establishes a relevant model category, but this passage does not establish when its obligations apply.

evidence.text: A Commission decision can also classify a GPAI model as systemic-risk on the basis of equivalent capabilities or impact, taking account of Annex XIII criteria.
evidence.quote: based on a decision of the Commission, ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel, it has capabilities or an impact equivalent to those set out in point (a) having regard to the criteria set out in Annex XIII.

credentials.credibility_notes: Defines an alternative route into the systemic-risk category rather than an application date or transitional rule.

evidence.text: Article 52 requires a provider whose GPAI model meets Article 51(1)(a)'s high-impact condition to notify the Commission without delay, and no later than two weeks after the condition is met or the provider knows it will be met.
evidence.quote: shall notify the Commission without delay and in any event within two weeks after that requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met.

credentials.credibility_notes: Establishes a specific Chapter V provider duty, but the present excerpt does not supply its application date or the transition for existing models.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR framework. A comprehensive search of government publications, intergovernmental organization reports, and academic literature was performed to identify relevant national and international guidelines. candidates.snippet: Objective Funnel plots (plots of effect estimates against sample size) may be useful to detect bias in meta-analyses that were later contradicted by large trials. candidates.title: DNA sequencing with chain-terminating inhibitors.
candidates.snippet: A new method for determining nucleotide sequences in DNA is described. It is similar to the "plus and minus" method [Sanger, F. & Coulson, A. R. (1975) J. Mol. Biol. 94, 441-448] but makes use of the 2',3'-dideoxy and arabinonucleoside analogues of the normal deoxynucleoside triphosphates, which act as specific chain-terminating inhibitors of DNA polymerase. The technique has been applied to the DNA of bacteriophage varphiX174 and is more rapid and more accurate than either the plus or the minus method.

candidates.title: Electrophoretic transfer of proteins from polyacrylamide gels to nitrocellulose sheets: procedure and some applications.
candidates.snippet: A method has been devised for the electrophoretic transfer of proteins from polyacrylamide gels to nitrocellulose sheets. The method results in quantitative transfer of ribosomal proteins from gels containing urea. For sodium dodecyl sulfate gels, the original band pattern was obtained with no loss of resolution, but the transfer was not quantitative. The method allows detection of proteins by autoradiography and is simpler than conventional procedures. The immobilized proteins were detectable by immunological procedures. All additional binding capacity on the nitrocellulose was blocked with excess protein; then a specific antibody was bound and, finally, a second antibody directed against the first antibody. The second antibody was either radioactively labeled or conjugated to fluorescein or to peroxidase. The specific protein was then detected by either autoradiography, under UV light, or by the peroxidase reaction product, respectively. In the latter case, as little as 100 pg of protein was clearly detectable. It is anticipated that the procedure will be applicable to analysis of a wide variety of proteins with specific reactions or ligands.

candidates.title: A global reference for human genetic variation.
candidates.snippet: The 1000 Genomes Project set out to provide a comprehensive description of common human genetic variation by applying whole-genome sequencing to a diverse set of individuals from multiple populations. Here we report completion of the project, having reconstructed the genomes of 2,504 individuals from 26 populations using a combination of low-coverage whole-genome sequencing, deep exome sequencing, and dense microarray genotyping. We characterized a broad spectrum of genetic variation, in total over 88 million variants (84.7 million single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), 3.6 million short insertions/deletions (indels), and 60,000 structural variants), all phased onto high-quality haplotypes. This resource includes >99% of SNP variants with a frequency of >1% for a variety of ancestries. We describe the distribution of genetic variation across the global sample, and discuss the implications for common disease studies.

candidates.title: The protein kinase homologue Ste20p is required to link the yeast pheromone response G-protein beta gamma subunits to downstream signalling components.
candidates.snippet: In the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae the G-protein beta gamma subunits have been shown to trigger downstream events of the pheromone response pathway. We have identified a new gene, designated STE20, which encodes a protein kinase homologue with sequence similarity to protein kinase C, which is required to transmit the pheromone signal from G beta gamma to downstream components of the signalling pathway. Overproduction of the kinase suppresses the mating defect of dominant-negative G beta mutations providing genetic evidence for an interaction with G beta, and epistasis experiments show that this kinase functions after or at the same point as G beta gamma, but before any of the other currently identified components of the signalling pathway. This points to a potentially new mechanism of G-protein mediated signal transduction, the activation of a protein kinase through G beta gamma.

candidates.title: SPIRIT 2013 explanation and elaboration: guidance for protocols of clinical trials.
candidates.snippet: High quality protocols facilitate proper conduct, reporting, and external review of clinical trials. However, the completeness of trial protocols is often inadequate. To help improve the content and quality of protocols, an international group of stakeholders developed the SPIRIT 2013 Statement (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials). The SPIRIT Statement provides guidance in the form of a checklist of recommended items to include in a clinical trial protocol.  This SPIRIT 2013 Explanation and Elaboration paper provides important information to promote full understanding of the checklist recommendations. For each checklist item, we provide a rationale and detailed description; a model example from an actual protocol; and relevant references supporting its importance. We strongly recommend that this explanatory paper be used in conjunction with the SPIRIT Statement. A website of resources is also available (www.spirit-statement.org). Complete documentation of key trial elements can facilitate transparency and protocol review for the benefit of all stakeholders.
